title: Blazing Saddles
about: A Black sheriff is sent to a racist frontier town as part of a scheme to drive everyone out.
cue: Serve the beans when the cowboys sit around the campfire.
faces: Serve the beans when the cowboys sit around the campfire.
“A man drink like that and he don't eat, he is going to DIE.” Sheriff Bart
Peanuts and pecans roasted with bourbon, brown sugar and smoked paprika
Cornbread baked in a hot iron pan, with chilli butter
Pinto beans simmered with bacon, molasses, mustard and smoked paprika
The cowboys' supper on the trail
Peaches and blackberries under a soft biscuit topping, sprinkled with raw sugar
Cinnamon apple filling in small shortcrust pies with pastry lids
Sarsaparilla poured over vanilla ice cream, with a dash of bitters
Poster and stills: TMDB. Bill no. 74. Talk of the town: It's Hedley, not Hedy. A toll booth in the middle of the desert.

Rock Ridge ChuckwagonBlazing SaddlesBeans. Lots of beans.Every recipe serves 4.

    StartersWaco Kid's whiskey nutsPeanuts and pecans roasted with bourbon, brown sugar and smoked paprikaHow to make it40g butter3 tbsp brown sugar1 tsp smoked paprika30ml bourbon200g peanuts150g pecansMelt the butter with the sugar, paprika and bourbon.Toss with the peanuts and pecans on a tray.Roast at 160°C, stirring once.Cool on the tray.Rock Ridge pan cornbreadCornbread baked in a hot iron pan, with chilli butterHow to make it200g fine polenta150g plain flour2 tsp baking powder1 tsp salt2 eggs375ml buttermilk100g butter1 long red chilli, finely choppedHeat the oven to 210°C with a 25cm cast iron pan inside.Mix the polenta, flour, baking powder and salt. Whisk the eggs into the buttermilk with 60g of the butter, melted, then stir into the dry mix.Take out the hot pan, swirl in a knob of butter and pour in the batter.Bake 20 to 22 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.Mash the rest of the butter with the chilli and a pinch of salt, and serve the cornbread in wedges with it.MainsCampfire smoky bacon baked beansPinto beans simmered with bacon, molasses, mustard and smoked paprikaHow to make it200g bacon1 brown onion2 tins of pinto beans400g crushed tomatoes3 tbsp molasses1 tbsp American mustard1 tsp smoked paprika250ml water150g cornmeal100g plain flour2 tsp baking powder250ml buttermilk1 egg80g butterDice the bacon and onion. Drain the beans.Fry the bacon and onion in a heavy pot until golden.Add the beans, tomatoes, molasses, mustard, paprika and water and simmer until thick.For the cornbread, mix the cornmeal, flour, baking powder, buttermilk, egg and melted butter.Pour into a hot buttered pan and bake at 220°C.Chuck wagon pepper rib eyesThe cowboys' supper on the trailHow to make itAs written, serves 4Rib eyes crusted with salt and cracked pepper, seared in cast iron over hot coals, with potatoes and onions fried in the butter and steak juices.Season 4 rib eyes of 300g heavily with salt and cracked pepper and leave 30 minutes.Boil 800g halved small potatoes for 10 minutes and drain.Sear the steaks in a smoking cast iron pan 3 to 4 minutes a side for medium-rare and rest 8 minutes.Add 50g butter and 2 sliced onions to the pan, then the potatoes, and fry 12 minutes until golden.Pour the resting juices over and serve.SweetsFrontier cobblerPeaches and blackberries under a soft biscuit topping, sprinkled with raw sugarHow to make it4 peaches250g blackberries80g caster sugar1 tbsp cornflour80g butter200g self-raising flour150ml full cream milk2 tbsp raw sugar300ml thickened creamSlice the peaches and toss with the blackberries, sugar and cornflour in a dish.Rub the butter into the flour, add the milk and drop over the fruit.Sprinkle with raw sugar and bake at 190°C.Serve with cream.Rock Ridge welcome pieCinnamon apple filling in small shortcrust pies with pastry lidsHow to make it3 Granny Smith apples30g butter50g caster sugar1 tsp cinnamon3 sheets of shortcrust pastry1 eggDice the apples and cook with the butter, sugar and cinnamon until soft. Cool.Cut rounds from the pastry, line a 12-hole tin, fill and lid with rounds from the third sheet.Egg wash and bake at 200°C.DrinksSaloon sarsaparilla spider floatSarsaparilla poured over vanilla ice cream, with a dash of bittersHow to make it4 x 375ml cans of sarsaparilla4 big scoops of vanilla ice cream8 dashes of aromatic bitters120ml bourbonChill the sarsaparilla.Put a big scoop of ice cream into each of four tall glasses.Pour the sarsaparilla slowly down the side so it foams up over the ice cream.Add a dash of bitters to each. For the cowboys, add bourbon before pouring. Serve with long spoons and straws.
